newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon sharply increases car import duties.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon sharply increases car import duties.

text.p: Lebanon's cabinet decided sharply to raise customs duty on imported cars, up to a maximum 200 percent.

Acting Finance Minister Fuoad Siniora was quoted on Wednesday as saying the new tax will be 20 percent on cars worth 15 million Lebanese pounds ($9,760), 50 percent on cars worth between 15 million pounds and 50 million, 100 percent on cars worth between 50 million pounds and 100 million and 200 percent on cars worth more than 100 million pounds.
Siniora said this decision, taken at a late night extraordinary meeting will have a positive effect on the environment, on the number of cars in the country and on the balance of payments.
Although Lebanon's balance of payments registered a surplus of $500 million for the first four months of 1997, customs said the trade deficit reached $1,482 million in the first quarter of the year.
"Lebanon's annual imported car bill is $800 million ... We import 75,000 cars a year and we have now about 1,300,000 cars which means a car for each three citizens," Siniora said.
Lebanon's population is estimated at 3.3 million. ($ = 1536 Lebanese Pounds)
